content: 1. The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced when used with indinavir. It is recommended to use a non-hormonal contraceptive method instead. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of etoposide by both inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Etravirine decreases indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism, making their concomitant use contraindicated unless indinavir is boosted with low-dose ritonavir. Indinavir also increases etravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative therapies or monitor closely. 6. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of everolimus by both inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Indinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 9. Famotidine decreases indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Fedratinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases fedratinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day and monitor for toxicities. 11. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of felbamate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while felodipine increases indinavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Indinavir increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 14. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (inhaled, intranasal, or furoate forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure, leading to adverse effects such as Cushing syndrome. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. 15. Indinavir increases the toxicity of fluvastatin, potentially due to OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Fluvoxamine increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Food decreases indinavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 18. Fosamprenavir and indinavir increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Fosaprepitant increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases fosaprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Fosphenytoin decreases indinavir levels by both inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Fostamatinib increases indinavir levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Indinavir also increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib's active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities and consider dose reductions. 22. Garlic decreases indinavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Indinavir increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Indinavir increases gentamicin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Indinavir increases gepirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Indinavir increases gilteritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related toxicities and adjust the dosage as needed. 27. Indinavir increases glasdegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 28. Indinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases indinavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Indinavir decreases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 30. Grapefruit increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Griseofulvin decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Indinavir increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 33. Indinavir increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Indinavir increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Indinavir increases hydrocortisone levels by both inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Indinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Indinavir increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 38. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
